summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of two kidney transplants, and recurrent UTIs was admitted for chills, cough, and cloudy urine. She was found to have a complicated urinary tract infection caused by ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli. She was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and later transitioned to oral cefpodoxime for a 14-day course. Blood cultures remained negative, and her symptoms resolved. A renal ultrasound showed elevated arterial velocities but no signs of rejection, with improved resistive indices. Her diabetes was poorly controlled, prompting an increase in Lantus insulin to 12 units at bedtime. She continued all home immunosuppressive and chronic medications. A chest X-ray revealed stable parenchymal changes, with follow-up CT recommended. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with transplant and endocrinology clinics and complete outpatient labs and imaging.
